prompt.en: The passage describes the angels as God's messengers who carry His commands, given wings for descending and ascending.

explanation.en: The essay glosses the verse's 'messengers' as intermediaries who carry God's commands, and reads their wings as given for descent and ascent, which is what the statement restates.

anchor.quote: He names the angels His messengers, intermediaries who carry His commands, given wings for descent and ascent

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, how do the Shia narrations read the mercy that no one can withhold in the second verse?

options.en: As the provision God sends down from sky and earth
Widely, counting temporary marriage and what flows on the Imam's tongue
As the true promise the world must not hide
As the blessing mankind is told to remember

explanation.en: The perspectives say the Shia narrations read this mercy widely: al-Sadiq is reported that temporary marriage is part of it, and that it is what God causes to flow upon the Imam's tongue.

anchor.quote: The Shia narrations read it more widely: al-Sadiq is reported saying that temporary marriage is part of this mercy, and that it is what God causes to flow upon the tongue of the Imam

prompt.en: If the people deny the Prophet, he is ____ that messengers before him were denied and all matters return to God.

explanation.en: The essay reads the verse as consolation for the Prophet: earlier messengers were also denied, and all matters return to God, so their denial need not weigh on him.

anchor.quote: If the people deny the Prophet, he is consoled that messengers before him were denied and all matters return to God

prompt.en: "Satan cannot gain mastery over the servant through whispering unless he has turned away from the remembrance of God." Who said this?

explanation.en: This is Imam al-Sadiq's teaching that Satan gains no power by whispering until the servant has turned from remembering God, made light of His prohibition, and forgotten that He knows his secret.

anchor.quote: Satan cannot gain mastery over the servant through whispering unless he has turned away from the remembrance of God

prompt.en: According to the essay, on what note does the passage close after naming Satan an enemy?

options.en: On God's mercy that no one can ever withhold
On Satan summoning his party to the Blaze
On the summons to remember Allah's blessing
Two promised ends: punishment for the faithless, reward for the faithful

explanation.en: The essay says the passage closes on its two promised ends: severe punishment for the faithless, and forgiveness with a great reward for the faithful who act well.

anchor.quote: the passage closes on its two promised ends: severe punishment for the faithless, forgiveness and a great reward for the faithful who act well

prompt.en: "Self-admiration has degrees; among them is that a servant's evil deed is made to seem fair to him." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about the self-admiration that spoils a deed, Imam al-Kazim said it has degrees, one being that a servant's evil deed is made to seem fair to him.

anchor.quote: self-admiration has degrees; among them is that a servant's evil deed is made to seem fair to him, so he sees it as good

prompt.en: According to Imam al-Sadiq, how does God begin to resurrect creation?

options.en: He raises them at the sound of the trumpet
He breathes life into them from His spirit
He sends rain from the sky for forty mornings
He commands the graves to open at once

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq said that when God wishes to resurrect creation He sends rain from the sky for forty mornings, so the joints come together and the flesh grows.

anchor.quote: When God wishes to resurrect the creation, He sends rain from the sky upon the earth for forty mornings, so the joints come together and the flesh grows.

prompt.en: One reading, from Qatada, takes its opening as a call to seek honour by ____.

explanation.en: The essay reports a reading from Qatada that takes the verse's opening as a call to seek honour by obeying God, since honour belongs wholly to Him.

anchor.quote: One reading, from Qatada, takes its opening as a call to seek honour by obeying God

prompt.en: The passage names only one thing that lengthens a person's life. What is it?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq said nothing increases life except maintaining kinship ties, so that keeping kin can add thirty years while cutting kinship off can take thirty away.

anchor.quote: We know of nothing that increases life except maintaining kinship ties, so that a man whose term is three years, being one who keeps kinship, God increases his life by thirty years

prompt.en: According to the passage, on the Day of Resurrection the idols will defend those who worshipped them.

explanation.en: The essay says that at the Resurrection the idols disown the worship offered them, and that they cannot even hear or answer, so they will not defend their worshippers.

anchor.quote: The idols people invoke own not a date-stone's husk; they neither hear nor answer, and at the Resurrection they disown the worship offered them.

prompt.en: And this is no hard thing for Him, which al-Tibyan glosses as not ____.

explanation.en: The verse says a new creation is no hard thing for God, and al-Tibyan glosses that phrase as not impossible, since nothing lies beyond His power.

anchor.quote: And this is no hard thing for Him, which al-Tibyan glosses as not impossible

prompt.en: "God does not seize the innocent for the guilty, nor punish children for the sins of the fathers." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked to explain 'No bearer shall bear another's burden,' Imam al-Sadiq said God does not seize the innocent for the guilty nor punish children for their fathers' sins.

anchor.quote: God does not seize the innocent for the guilty, nor punish children for the sins of the fathers

prompt.en: According to the essay, what do the contrasts like blind and seer, darkness and light stand for?

options.en: The rich Lord set against needy creation
The Quran set against the earlier scriptures
The believer set against the disbeliever
The living set against those in the graves

explanation.en: The essay says the run of contrasts are parables, al-Tibyan explains, for the believer and the disbeliever, so seer, light and life stand for faith against unbelief.

anchor.quote: These are parables, al-Tibyan explains, for the believer and the disbeliever, faith set against unbelief

prompt.en: The passage limits the Prophet's charge to warning, not to compelling anyone to believe.

explanation.en: The essay says the Prophet cannot make the dead-hearted deniers hear, so he is charged only to warn; making anyone believe is not his task.

anchor.quote: So the Prophet is charged only to warn

prompt.en: According to the passage, how do the Shia sources read the warner sent to every nation?

options.en: That the Prophet is the only warner God ever sent
That every age has its own Imam
That the warner for each nation is the Quran itself
That each nation's warner brought a new scripture

explanation.en: The Shia sources carry the warner into every age, glossing the verse as 'for every age there is an Imam,' the one who interprets the Quran, Ali.

anchor.quote: The Shia sources carry the warner into every age. al-Burhan, transmitting Ali ibn Ibrahim, glosses the verse as 'for every age there is an Imam'

prompt.en: According to the essay, what does the great variety of colors in fruits, mountains and people show?

options.en: That every plant draws on the same seed
That divine ordering, not water alone, is at work
That water is the single cause of all life
That color has no meaning in creation

explanation.en: The essay argues that if water alone produced them, all would be one color; their differing hues instead point to divine ordering at work behind creation.

anchor.quote: Were these merely the yield of one cause, water, they would all be one color; their difference points to divine ordering at work

prompt.en: "By 'the learned' is meant one whose deed confirms his word." Who is reported to have defined the learned this way?

explanation.en: Asked about God's learned servants who truly fear Him, Imam al-Sadiq said the learned is one whose deed confirms his word, and one whose deed does not is not learned.

anchor.quote: By 'the learned' is meant one whose deed confirms his word; and whoever's deed does not confirm his word is not learned.

prompt.en: The grief is what befell them in the world, of ____.

explanation.en: Imam al-Baqir explained that the grief God removes from the people of Paradise is the fear and hardship they had suffered in the world.

anchor.quote: The grief is what befell them in the world, of fear and hardship.

prompt.en: In the essay, what are the faithless told when they beg to be brought back to act righteously?

options.en: Their punishment will be eased in time
They may return once they repent
They had a life long enough to heed, and a warner came
No warner was ever sent to them

explanation.en: The essay says those who cry to be brought back are told they had a life long enough to take admonition and that the warner had already come to them.

anchor.quote: they cry to be brought back to act righteously and are answered that they were given a life long enough to heed and that the warner had come

prompt.en: In the Shia reports, the one who takes the lead in all good works is someone who merely knows the Imam.

explanation.en: In the Shia reports the one foremost in all good works is the Imam himself; the one who merely knows the Imam is the average, not the foremost.

anchor.quote: The Shia reports make the chosen the Prophet's household: the foremost is the Imam, the average is one who knows the Imam, and the wrongdoer is one who does not know him

prompt.en: The commentary says God's knowledge of what is in the breasts means He will hold people to account for their inner belief and deeds.

explanation.en: The essay says God's knowledge of the Unseen and of what is in the breasts is a warning that He will judge people and call them to account for their inner belief and deeds, so the claim holds.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai reads this as a warning that He will judge people by what their inner belief and deeds hold, and call them to account for it

prompt.en: According to the essay, what does the challenge to the idolaters about their 'partners' prove?

options.en: That the partners hold a share in the heavens
That the idolaters were given a clear scripture
That a lord must be a creator, and the partners created nothing
That the partners deserve some worship

explanation.en: The essay reads the challenge as proof that a lord must be a creator; the partners created no part of the earth and hold no share in the heavens, so they cannot be lords.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai frames this as a proof that a lord must be a creator, whose claim would need evidence from the world or a revealed scripture, neither of which exists

prompt.en: "Allah is the carrier of the Throne, the heavens and the earth and all that is in them and between them." Who said this?

explanation.en: Answering al-Jathaliq, Imam Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, said Allah carries the Throne, the heavens and the earth, citing the verse that Allah sustains them lest they fall apart.

anchor.quote: Allah is the carrier of the Throne, the heavens and the earth and all that is in them and between them

prompt.en: On 'evil schemes beset only their authors,' both traditions draw the same ____ from the Book.

explanation.en: The perspectives say that on this verse both traditions draw the same triad from the Book: scheming, transgression, and breaking a pledge, three acts that recoil on the one who commits them.

anchor.quote: both traditions draw the same triad from the Book

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does Tabatabai understand the respite God grants before the appointed term?

options.en: A sign the schemers have been forgiven
Proof the Hour will never arrive
A reward granted for their solemn oaths
A worldly reprieve until death or the Resurrection

explanation.en: The essay says that if God punished people at once for what they earned He would leave no creature on the earth; instead He grants a worldly respite until death or the Resurrection.

anchor.quote: for Tabatabai a worldly respite until death or the Resurrection
